# dsh-auto-review-model-router

Route DSH's experimental **auto-review** safety gate to a model you choose, so a
premium agent model
does not pay for its own safety reviews.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

With that entry every review runs on `deepseek-official/deepseek-flash` while the
agent keeps `claud
e-opus-4`, `gpt-6-astra`, or whatever else the session selected.
## The problem it solves

`@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-auto-review` reviews each gated tool call by
calling `ctx.llm.stream(

)` on **the session's own route**: it copies `provider`
and `model` out of the session request heade

r
(`snapshotAutoReview()` in `packages/experimental/auto-review/src/index.ts`).
There is no `reviewM

odel` field in the shipped plugin, so an expensive agent
model is charged for one extra full review
request per gated call.
## How it works

The plugin wraps two service methods at activation: `llm.stream` always, and
`llm.prepareCall` unles
s `wrapPrepareCall` is off.

1. A request is recognized as an auto-review call when it is **hand-built**
(it does not carry the a

gent loop's own-request mark) **and** its `system`
prompt starts with auto-review's fixed `REVIEW_PO

LICY` opening. Only such a
request is ever rewritten.
2. It is copied onto `reviewModel`, and the so

urce route's `reasoningEffort` and
`maxTokens` are dropped. Both are properties of the *agent's* mod

el: a
reasoning effort the target does not declare makes the harness throw
`UNSUPPORTED_REASONING_EF

FORT`, and an inherited output cap can exceed the
target's limit. Either would fail every review clo

sed.
3. Everything else — the review prompt, its policy system prompt, `temperature`,
and the `{"ris

k":…,"decision":…}` JSON protocol the gate parses — is
unchanged. Only the model that produces the v

erdict changes.
4. A review that fails transiently is retried on the same route
(`retryAttempts`, de

fault 4). The gate calls `llm.stream` directly, outside
the agent loop, so the harness retry plugin

(an `agent/request-error`
listener) never sees a review: without this, one dropped connection denies

est-error`
listener) never sees a review: without this, one dropped connection denies
the tool call.
### Why retries need their own classification

Only the codes the harness itself treats as transient are retried:
`EMPTY_RESPONSE`, `RATE_LIMIT`, `

SERVER`, `TRANSPORT`. `TIMEOUT` is deliberately
excluded — the DeepSeek adapter raises it from an **

idle watchdog**, so retrying
it multiplies a silent wait by the attempt count while the auto-review

deadline
drains. `ABORTED` (the deadline, or the caller cancelling) and configuration
errors such as
`AUTH` are not fixed by trying again.

A failed attempt's terminal `finish` chunk is held back: the gate's reader ends
the review on any te

rminal `finish`, so yielding it would end the review on the
first transport blip. Reasoning chunks s

tay live (the reader ignores reasoning
content), so a retried review exposes more than one attempt's

reasoning while the
verdict is still parsed from the final text block alone.
### Why the wrappers, and not an `llm/stream` listener
Two seams were tried first and both are dead ends on a real runtime:

- Mutating the request inside an `llm/stream` listener throws: auto-review
freezes it (`deepFreeze`)

before streaming.
- Returning `next(replacement)` from a listener never reaches the adapter:
Cordis

's `EventsService.waterfall` invokes the innermost callback with the
argument list it closed over.
-

Writing `ctx.llm.stream = wrapper` is also ineffective: `ctx.llm` is a
per-read traceable proxy, an
d its property overlay shadows what you write.

The wrappers are therefore installed on the object that owns each method in the
service's prototype

chain (`LlmRuntime.prototype` in practice), which is the one
seam every consumer actually calls. Bot

h are removed when the plugin's fiber
disposes.
### Why `prepareCall` needs its own wrapper

A prepared handle resolves its route during `prepareCall` and then rejects a
dispatch whose config d

iffers from the resolved one
(`INVALID_PREPARED_CALL`). The retarget must therefore happen *before*

the call
is prepared; swapping the route in the returned handle cannot work. With
`wrapPrepareCall:

true` (the default) a review prepared that way runs on the
review route, and turning it off restores
the session route for that path.
## Install
Published on npm as `dsh-auto-review-model-router`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
From a local checkout instead, link it:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then insert it in the profile patch layer, after the auto-review bundle:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Restart the app: patch-layer changes apply at profile startup.
## Configuration
| Field | Default | Meaning |
| `reviewModel` | `deepseek-official/deepseek-flash` | `<provider>/<model>` every review runs on. An

empty string disables routing. |
| `systemPromptPatterns` | the shipped `REVIEW_POLICY` opening | S
ubstrings, or `/regex/u` literals, matched against a request's `system` prompt. Widen this only if a

harness release rewrites that prompt. |
| `retryAttempts` | `4` | Retries after the first attempt o

f one review call, so up to 5 attempts. `0` disables retrying. Maximum 10. |
| `retryDelayMs` | `500

` | Pause before each retry. |
| `wrapPrepareCall` | `true` | Also route review requests issued thro

ugh `llm.prepareCall`. |
| `dropReasoningEffort` | `true` | Drop the source route's reasoning effort

on the review request. |
| `dropMaxTokens` | `true` | Drop the source route's output cap on the rev

iew request. |
| `logRetargets` | `true` | Log each retargeted review. Retries log a warning regardl

quest. |
| `logRetargets` | `true` | Log each retargeted review. Retries log a warning regardless. |
## Verify

The test suite has two files. `test/router.test.js` covers the decision surface
with no harness at a

ll; `test/live.test.js` runs the wrappers over the real
`LlmRuntime` and skips those checks when nei

ther this package nor
`DSH_PROFILE_DIR` resolves `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm`.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Two commands rather than `node --test`: each file runs its `node:test` suite
in-process, while `node
--test` spawns a child process per file.
